title: The Exact Price of a Phase Shift
description: LaTeX source, numerical checks (456) and a Lean 4 certificate (95 theorems) of the finite and algebraic parts of the paper The Exact Price of a Phase Shift. The paper proves that a passive causal system without zeros in the upper half-plane cannot shift every frequency of a band [a,b] by the same phase theta > 0 without loss: its mean attenuation over the band is at least theta (K(kappa) - E(kappa))/kappa nepers, kappa = (b-a)/(b+a), and an explicit system has the least attenuation at every frequency of the band at once. On a union of several bands the least mean loss is theta Lambda_B, with an explicit constant Lambda_B attained by an explicit system with one resonance in each gap, and it exceeds the sum of the single-band prices. With zeros allowed, one explicit system with a single zero has the least attenuation at every frequency at once. With a delay added to the phase, the least mean loss without zeros is found in closed form and stays above a positive floor; with zeros the optimal system exists, is unique and its loss falls exponentially with the delay.
